text: Brightleaf Fitness runs forty studios plus a mobile app on one legacy SQL Server database -- and three teams who each built their own 'active member' logic independently now report three different numbers for the same company.

Finance counts anyone not canceled. Marketing counts anyone active in the app in the last thirty days. Product counts active studio-location rows -- and double-counts members who belong to two locations.
Here's Finance's actual query: anyone whose subscription status isn't canceled counts as active, including members who've simply paused their membership.
Marketing's query only counts recent check-ins -- a different, narrower question entirely. Product's query joins through a newer table that quietly counts some members twice.
Three reasonable rules, zero agreement, and one confirmed bug. Next: turning this audit into one testable definition everyone signs off on.
